newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai steel group seeking protection from cheap imports.
newsitem.headline: Thai steel group seeking protection from cheap imports.

text.p: Sahaviriya Steel Industries Plc, hit by high imports of cheap hot-rolled coil steel, said on Friday it hopes the new Thai government will work to protect local industry from cheap imports.

"I'm confident that the new government will come up with a positive action which will protect local industry," Adisak Lowjun, president of Sahaviriya Steel Industries -- Thailand's sole producer of hot-rolled coil steel -- told a news conference.
A new government headed by New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is due to be sworn in on Sunday.
"The excessive imports of the cheap metal, mainly from Russia and Ukraine, have affected our company's business," Adisak said.
Adisak said the company hopes an investigation it requested into heavy dumping of imported steel will be completed late next month.

A separate request was filed by the company to the state-run Board of Investment (BOI) to impose a heavier surcharge on the metal imports. Presently, Thailand imposes a 10 percent duty on imported hot-rolled coil steel.
The company has asked the BOI to impose a 50 percent surcharge on the imported steel.
Adisak said the price of imported hot-rolled coil steel was between $240-$250 per tonne while his company was charging around $323 per tonne.
"The company cannot lower its price more than this and the only way out for the company to survive is to cut its production," said Adisak.
He said the company's maximum total production capacity is 2.4 million tonnes annually.

But the company was now producing at around 110,000 tonnes a month, almost half its maximum production capacity, because of a lack of purchasing orders due to the heavy dumping of imported steel and the country's sluggish economic conditions, Adisak said.
Sahaviriya on Friday reported sharply weaker financial results for the first three quarters of the year.
It posted a loss of 1.64 billion baht ($65.6 billion) or 3.21 baht a share in the first nine months compared to a profit of 120.69 million or 0.24 baht a share in the same period last year.
The company's total sales during the first nine months of 1996 amounted to 7.4 billion baht compared to 7.3 billion baht in the same period last year.

Adisak said his company expected that its exports, chiefly to Asian countries and Australia, would account for about 15 percent of its total production this year. It has planned to increase its exports to 20 percent of total production in 1997.

He also said Sahaviriya has signed an agreement with Japanese steelmaker NKK Corp for NKK to provide technical training to two of Sahaviriya's affiliates -- Thai Coated Steel Co Ltd and Thai Cold Rolled Steel Sheet Plc -- starting in January.

Thai Coated Steel, established in early 1994, has an annual total production capacity of 240,000 tonnes of coated steel. Thai Cold Rolled Steel Sheet will have an annual production output of 1.2 million tonnes after its plant starts operation around the middle of 1997.
Sahaviriya Steel's share price was trading at a new year low of 8.80 baht, down 0.20, at 0830 GMT.
(US$1 = 25 baht)
-- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
